data.one_liner: Sends Modbus requests to remote devices via TCP/IP connections.
data.what_it_does: Implements the Modbus TCP protocol for sending requests to remote devices over ethernet networks. It provides various Modbus element types like registers, coils, and discrete inputs, alongside auto-connection modes, timeout settings, and server discovery.
use_when: You need to communicate with industrial devices or servers using Modbus TCP/IP.
You want support for various data element types like numeric registers, bit masks, enums, and file records.
avoid_when: You are communicating over Serial ports or UDP instead of TCP/IP (use companion packages instead).
You do not need industrial Modbus protocol support.
strengths: Includes built-in server discovery and connection timeout features for TCP.
Offers a rich variety of typed Modbus elements with built-in byte endianness and scaling support.
weaknesses: Limited specifically to TCP/IP; requires separate packages for UDP or Serial communications.
Relies heavily on external Modbus server implementations and proper network configurations.
data.setup_notes: Add the package to pubspec.yaml and configure network permissions for TCP/IP socket access on target platforms.
